concepts.title: Area of a Trapezium
concepts.definition: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides, and its area is half the sum of the parallel sides times the distance between them - the average of the parallel sides spread over the height.
concepts.key_idea: Average of parallel sides times height: (a + b)/2 times h.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh109.txt section 9.2 (area of a trapezium, examples)

solution_steps.explain: Half the sum times the height gives the area.

concepts.title: Area of a General Polygon by Splitting
concepts.definition: Any polygon yields its area when split into friendly shapes - triangles, rectangles, trapeziums - on a suitable base line; computing each part and adding them gives the whole area, the standard trick for irregular fields.
concepts.key_idea: Cut the awkward figure into shapes you know, then add the areas.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh109.txt section 9.2 (area of a polygon by splitting into known shapes)

solution_steps.explain: Draw one diagonal or base on which the parts stand.
Triangles use half base times height; trapeziums use the average formula.
The sum rebuilds the full polygon area.

concepts.title: Surface Area of Cube, Cuboid and Cylinder
concepts.definition: Surface area wraps the solid: a cuboid needs 2(lw + wh + hl) covering all six faces, a cube is 6 times its edge squared, and a cylinder takes the two circle ends plus the rolled rectangle, 2 pi r times (r + h).
concepts.formula: surface = 2 * (length * width + width * height + height * length)
concepts.key_idea: Unfold the solid into its net; the net's area is the surface area.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh109.txt sections 9.4 (surface areas of cube, cuboid, cylinder)

solution_steps.explain: lw, wh and hl are the three distinct rectangles.
solution_steps.compute: faces = length * width + width * height + height * length

solution_steps.explain: Each face appears twice in the box.

concepts.title: Volume of Cube, Cuboid and Cylinder
concepts.definition: Volume counts the unit cubes inside a solid: a cuboid holds length times width times height of them, a cube repeats its edge thrice, and a cylinder stacks pi r squared circle layers up its height.
concepts.key_idea: Base area times height fills any prism-like solid, cylinder included.

concepts.title: Volume of a Cylinder and Capacity
concepts.definition: A cylinder's volume is the circle base times the height - pi times radius squared times height - and capacity measures the same volume in litres, with one cubic centimetre holding one millilitre.
concepts.key_idea: Circle area pi r squared stacked up the height; 1000 cubic cm equals one litre.

solution_steps.explain: Base area times height is the volume.
